title: Wood's church background and rural Virginia roots
summary: Wood moved from Baptist to Presbyterian to Episcopalian, explains his Fluvanna County roots, and Allen mentions Paul Crawford's hymn knowledge.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well, I grew up in the Baptist church and I became a Presbyterian and then I became an Episcopalian.
That's quite a bit of change.
Which, but, yeah. I still, you know, I guess I like the music in my rural Virginia Baptist church better than I like it in my Episcopal church where I really am well placed and established.
Rural Virginia? I thought you were from Richmond.

Well, I have a dual background. I have deep roots in Fluvanna County, Virginia. As well as in Richmond. I spent time in both places. I was born in Richmond, but my family, my grandparents on both sides lived in Fluvanna. And I spent all the summers up there and from time to time lived there as my mother drifted back and forth between the city and the country. So, but I, I, I went, I graduated from high school in Richmond, but I, when I was, my boyhood and early teen years I was in Fluvanna as much as I was in Richmond. And so I have those deep rural roots.

So, the more evangelical Protestant type of faith ties in with all those hymns, I guess. I mean, that's what, that's my guess. Yeah. And probably one of the reasons why I like them.
